small_guidance:
- The GEMM is 128×16384×16384 — M=128 is tiny, so favor configs with BLOCK_M=64 or 128 and large BLOCK_N (256) / BLOCK_K (64-128); drop the BLOCK_M=64,BLOCK_N=128 configs and add (BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=256, BLOCK_K=64, num_warps=8, num_stages=4) and (BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=256, BLOCK_K=128, num_warps=8, num_stages=3).
- Softmax: BLOCK_N=2048 forces 8 sequential iterations over N=16384; bump BLOCK_N to 4096 or 8192 with num_warps=16, num_stages=2 to halve the loop trips, and pre-load once into registers if you make it single-pass.
- The two-pass softmax re-reads the input from DRAM; cache the post-GEMM tile or fuse the softmax row-max accumulation into the GEMM epilogue by writing per-N-tile partial (max, sumexp) into a small scratch and finishing in a tiny second kernel.
large_guidance:
- Fuse dropout + softmax into a single persistent row kernel: launch one program per row (128 rows total), each holding the full 16384-wide row in registers/SMEM across 8 warps, applying dropout scale+mask and computing softmax in one online pass with no second read of the row.
- Since M=128 is small and N=K=16384, consider a split-K GEMM (or a Stream-K style) so the 128 SMs on the 4090 are saturated — the current grid is only ⌈128/BLOCK_M⌉·⌈16384/BLOCK_N⌉ ≈ 2·64 = 128 tiles, which is fine, but split-K with atomics or a 2-stage reduce can overlap better at this skinny shape.
- Eliminate the softmax read-back entirely by writing the GEMM output tile already biased+dropped to SMEM/global, and have the softmax kernel be persistent per-row consuming tiles as they land; alternatively, since out_features fits a row tile across warps, do GEMM-then-softmax fused: each program computes one full row of the output (K loop reused) and immediately softmaxes — turning two kernels into one.
